Review.Independence: Independent review: I did not see the authoring conversation, notes.md or the brief. I was given contract.xml revision 1, the grace5-review skill, evidence-records.md, the five cited rule files, the complete git diff bbea8489..ffde347b (15 files, 311 insertions, read in full), receipts run-1.xml and run-2.xml with all ten logs, and the live outputs of bun src/cli.ts status and check. To judge behaviour I also read the modules the tool imports (src/upgrade/skills.ts, src/upgrade/pin.ts, kernelVersion in src/records.ts), src/tools/package.ts, tsconfig.json, and the existing upgrade conformance tests. The whole diff was covered; nothing was missing.

Finding.Text: The new suite exercises the main failure paths (corruption fails and names the path, restore passes, project-owned skill ignored, missing packaged source errors, --help), but two documented failure paths of the tool have no test: the unreadable-pin branch, where installationHealth catches readPin's throw and must report state: unreadable with code 1, and the usage errors that exit 2 (unknown argument, --root without a value). No required check covers them either: CK5's live pin is a valid 0.8.0 and CK4 runs only --help, so a regression that swallowed the pin error into a pass would stay green. readPin's throw itself is proven by UP-16, so only the tool's own wiring is uncovered. Add a temp-root case writing a non-version pin under .grace5/kernel-version and expecting code 1 with the unreadable line, and a spawn case expecting exit 2 for an unknown argument.

Review.Adequacy: bun run check is tsc --noEmit with tsconfig include ["src"], so the new tool, its test and every imported kernel module type-check under strict together with the rest of the kernel (A6). A type error in installation-health.ts or in its use of skillDifferences/readPin fails the command; run-2's log shows a clean exit 0. A pass separates compiling code from the broken-import or type-error failure mode.

bun test --parallel ran 104 tests across 13 files in run-2 (103 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail) against 99 across 12 in run-1: exactly the five new tests and their 14 expect() calls. They assert the failure paths, not just the happy path: a corrupted installed SKILL.md yields drift: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, installation: drift and exit 1, restoring the exact bytes yields exit 0, a project-owned skill beside the installed ones is ignored, a missing packaged source returns code 1 with the actionable line, and --help prints usage with exit 0, all in throwaway tmpdir roots in both skill locations. The pre-existing UP-07/UP-19 conformance cases cover the framework side of A1: refresh is idempotent, repairs drift, creates no location and leaves project-owned skills byte-identical. The client mirror generator itself is out of this repository by N5, so its discipline is guidance-bound and its violations are detectable by the health tool. Residual untested branches are recorded as non-blocking F1.

bun run package:verify regenerates all three packages from skills/ and the CLI reference from the help text in memory and compares byte for byte, reporting drift per missing, changed or extra file and failing on any difference or stray entry. Run-2's log shows ok claude-plugin, ok openpackage, ok skills, ok cli-reference. A pass therefore separates current generated artifacts from stale or hand-edited ones after the guidance edits (A5), and proves the new prepare/execute bullets propagated identically to every package (the propagation side of A4); whether the prose states the ownership and freshness rules is judged by this review's reading of the diff, which it does.

bun src/tools/installation-health.ts --help failed in the start run (module not found, exit 1) and passed in run-2 with exit 0 and the full usage text in the log. A pass separates an existing, runnable tool with working argument handling from the missing-tool or crash failure mode; the usage content itself is additionally asserted by CK2's --help test, so a silent exit-0 stub would not survive the check set.

bun src/tools/installation-health.ts at the repository root passed in run-2 on the final candidate with kernel: 0.8.0, state: 0.8.0, installed skills: none, exit 0. This repository installs no package-owned skill (only the local, non-packaged grace5-release under .agents/skills), so the pass honestly exercises the documented none branch: it proves the tool runs against the live root, reads the real pin, and correctly leaves a non-packaged grace5-* directory alone instead of claiming ownership of it or reporting false drift. The corruption/restore semantics on installed bytes cannot be exercised here because nothing package-owned is installed; CK2's temp-root tests discriminate those, and CK5 is the fresh handoff evaluation of the live installation state, re-run in the final run rather than carried over, as D2 and the new source-identity paragraph require.
Review.Rule: K1: the exclusion rule is untouched; installed packaged directories remain kernel-managed and outside the candidate. The tool only reads them and the pin (existsSync, statSync, readdirSync, readFileSync via skillDifferences and readPin) and contains no write call, so it writes no source path; the tests write only under os.tmpdir(). The added paragraph states the excluded-input freshness rule and the bounded-fingerprint admission path without adding any fingerprint, matching the rule file's own text. CK5 executes a source-path tool, not a file kept in a kernel-managed path.

K2: the refresh remains the only writer of installed packaged skills; the diff adds no writer, no STEPS change, no migration boundary and no table row, and the tool reuses the refresh's read-only comparison (skillDifferences) with the same scope, leaving non-packaged grace5-* directories alone as the migration rules already require. The new package-ownership section states the ownership and handoff-freshness rules consistently with the release sections. Release discipline holds: package.json stays 0.8.0, .grace5/kernel-version, the README status line and the migration table are untouched, no tag points at either revision, and the single commit ffde347 carries the Change trailer; drift is reported, never repaired (N1, D4).

K3: an installation-health pass substitutes for nothing. CK5 is itself a required check bound by approval-1.xml, whose five Bound hashes equal the definition hashes printed by check, and it was freshly evaluated in run-2 on the final candidate with its own receipt; the guidance states explicitly that health is not candidate evidence, not an approval and not a receipt. Boundary: status reports no outside: and no protected: path; every diff path lies in Affected or in the change's own records directory (kernel-managed, excluded), and no Protected path is touched.

K4: exactly one entry, L-28, is added for the installation-health mechanism with all seven columns: source is the observed failure P-017 named in the contract's Problem, smallest alternative, expected benefit, cost (one read-only tool and one rule), and a removal criterion (two cycles without drift found at handoff). No fingerprint mechanism is added or entered, per N2/D3.

K5: an ordinary change. No version, pin, tag, migration row or release moves; the new mechanism is documented in a method topic file (upgrade.md) and carries its ledger entry, and the Problem cites an observed failure, satisfying the surface rule. The generated-artifact rule is honored: skills/ was edited and all three packages plus the CLI reference regenerated and verified by CK3. The contract's 644 words against the 600 target are reported, not enforced (L-03), and were approved.
